title: Port types, component types and test configurations

sentences.text: TTCN-3 allows the (dynamic) specification of concurrent test configurations (or configuration for short).

A configuration consists of a set of inter-connected test components with well-defined communication ports and an explicit test system interface which defines the borders of the test system (see figure 4).
NOTE: Additional configuration and deployment support for TTCN-3 is defined in the optional package [i.11].
TTCN Test system
**MTC** **PTC1**

Abstract Test System Interface
                               Real Test System Interface
**SUT**
**Figure 4: Conceptual view of a typical TTCN-3 test configuration**
Within every configuration there shall be one (and only one) Main Test Component (MTC).
Test components that are not MTCs are called parallel test components or PTCs.
The MTC shall be created by the system automatically at the start of each test case execution.
The behaviour defined in the body of the test case shall execute on this component.
During execution of a test case, other components can be created dynamically by the explicit use of the create operation.
Test case execution shall end when the MTC terminates.
All other PTCs are treated equally i.e. there is no explicit hierarchical relationship among them and the termination of a single PTC terminates neither other components nor the MTC.
When the MTC terminates, the test system has to stop all PTCs not terminated by the moment when the test case execution is ended.
Communication between test components and between the components and the test system interface is achieved via communication ports (see clause 9.1).
Test component types and port types, denoted by the keywords component and port, shall be defined in the module definitions part.
The actual configuration of components and the connections between them is achieved by performing create and connect operations within the test case behaviour.
The component ports are connected to the ports of the test system interface by means of the map operation (see clause 21.1.1).
Test components are connected via their ports, i.e. connections among components and between a component and the test system interface are port-oriented.
Each port is modelled as an infinite FIFO queue which stores the incoming messages or procedure calls until they are processed by the component owning that port (see figure 5).
NOTE: While TTCN-3 ports are infinite in principle in a real test system they may overflow.
This is to be treated as a test case error (see clause 24.1).
**MTC** **PTC**
**Figure 5: The TTCN-3 communication port model**
TTCN-3 connections are port-to-port and port-to-test system interface connections (see figure 6).
There are no restrictions on the number of connections a component may maintain.
One-to-many connections are also allowed (e.g. figure 6 (g) or (h)).
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:
a) The following connections are not allowed (see figure 7):
A port owned by a component A shall not be connected with two or more ports owned by the same component (figure 7 (a) and (e)).
MTC; Col2; PTC
A port of a test system interface cannot have connection with more than one port owned by a component A. This means, connections as shown in figure 7 (b) are not allowed.
A port owned by a component A shall not be connected with two or more ports owned by a component B (see figure 7 (c)).
A port owned by a component A can only have a one-to-one connection with the test system interface.
This means, connections as shown in figure 7 (d) are not allowed.
Connections within the test system interface are not allowed (see figure 7 (f)).
A port that is connected shall not be mapped and a port that is mapped shall not be connected (see figure 7 (g)).
b) Since TTCN-3 allows dynamic configurations and addresses, the restrictions on connections cannot always be checked at compile-time.
The checks shall be made at runtime and shall lead to a test case error when failing.

TTCN-3 is used to test implementations.
The object being tested is known as the Implementation Under Test or IUT.
The IUT may offer direct interfaces for testing or it may be part of system in which case the tested object is known as a System Under Test or SUT.
In the minimal case the IUT and the SUT are equivalent.
In the present document the term SUT is used in a general way to mean either SUT or IUT.
In a real test environment test cases need to communicate with the SUT.
However, the specification of the real physical connection is outside the scope of TTCN-3.
Instead, a well defined (but abstract) test system interface shall be associated with each test case.
A test system interface definition is identical to a component definition, i.e. it is a list of all possible communication ports through which the test case is connected to the SUT.
The test system interface statically defines the number and type of the port connections to the SUT during a test run.

However, the connections between the test system interface and the TTCN-3 test components are dynamic in nature and may be modified during a test run by using map and unmap operations (see clause 21.1).

A component type definition is used to define the test system interface because, conceptually, component type definitions and test system interface definitions have the same form (both are collections of ports defining possible connection points).
When used as test system interfaces, components cannot make use of any constants, variables and timers declared in the component type.
The same as a component type definition (see clause 6.2.10.1).
Generally, a component type reference defining the test system interface shall be associated with every test case using more than one test component.
The ports of the test system interface shall automatically be instantiated by the system together with the MTC when the test case execution starts.
The operation returning the component reference of the test system interface is system.
This shall be used to address the ports of the test system.
In the case where the MTC is the only component that is instantiated during test execution, a test system interface need not be associated to the test case.
In this case, the component type definition associated with the MTC implicitly defines the corresponding test system interface.
Variables, timers and constants declared in component types, which are used as test system interfaces will have no effect.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:
a) The same as for component type definitions (see clause 6.2.10.1).

requirements.subject: ent:test-configuration
requirements.canonical: A test configuration IS a concurrent test configuration whose specification in TTCN-3 MAY be dynamic.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows the (dynamic) specification of concurrent test configurations (or configuration for short).

requirements.subject: ent:test-configuration
requirements.canonical: A test configuration IS a set of inter-connected test components with well-defined communication ports and an explicit test system interface.
requirements.original: A configuration consists of a set of inter-connected test components with well-defined communication ports and an explicit test system interface which defines the borders of the test system (see figure 4).

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.canonical: The test system interface IS the entity that defines the borders of the test system.
requirements.original: A configuration consists of a set of inter-connected test components with well-defined communication ports and an explicit test system interface which defines the borders of the test system (see figure 4).

requirements.subject: ent:test-configuration
requirements.canonical: A test configuration SHALL contain exactly one Main Test Component (MTC).
requirements.original: Within every configuration there shall be one (and only one) Main Test Component (MTC).

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.canonical: A test component that is not the MTC IS a parallel test component (PTC).
requirements.original: Test components that are not MTCs are called parallel test components or PTCs.

requirements.subject: ent:mtc
requirements.canonical: The MTC SHALL be created automatically by the test system at the start of each test case execution.
requirements.original: The MTC shall be created by the system automatically at the start of each test case execution.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: The behaviour defined in the body of a test case SHALL execute on the MTC.
requirements.original: The behaviour defined in the body of the test case shall execute on this component.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: During test case execution, test components other than the MTC CAN be created dynamically by explicit use of the `create` operation.
requirements.original: During execution of a test case, other components can be created dynamically by the explicit use of the create operation.

requirements.subject: ent:test-case-execution
requirements.canonical: Test case execution SHALL end when the MTC terminates.
requirements.original: Test case execution shall end when the MTC terminates.

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.canonical: A PTC IS NOT in an explicit hierarchical relationship with any other PTC.
requirements.original: All other PTCs are treated equally i.e. there is no explicit hierarchical relationship among them and the termination of a single PTC terminates neither other components nor the MTC.

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.canonical: The termination of a single PTC IS NOT terminating any other test component.
requirements.original: All other PTCs are treated equally i.e. there is no explicit hierarchical relationship among them and the termination of a single PTC terminates neither other components nor the MTC.

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.canonical: The termination of a single PTC IS NOT terminating the MTC.
requirements.original: All other PTCs are treated equally i.e. there is no explicit hierarchical relationship among them and the termination of a single PTC terminates neither other components nor the MTC.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.canonical: When the MTC terminates, the test system SHALL stop all PTCs that are not yet terminated when the test case execution ends.
requirements.original: When the MTC terminates, the test system has to stop all PTCs not terminated by the moment when the test case execution is ended.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: Communication between test components and between test components and the test system interface IS performed via communication ports.
requirements.original: Communication between test components and between the components and the test system interface is achieved via communication ports (see clause 9.1).

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.canonical: A component type (keyword `component`) SHALL be defined in the module definitions part.
requirements.original: Test component types and port types, denoted by the keywords component and port, shall be defined in the module definitions part.

ambiguity.issue: 'Test component types' is used where the standard elsewhere says 'component type'.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type (keyword `port`) SHALL be defined in the module definitions part.
requirements.original: Test component types and port types, denoted by the keywords component and port, shall be defined in the module definitions part.

requirements.subject: ent:test-configuration
requirements.canonical: The actual test configuration of test components and the connections between them IS established by performing `create` and `connect` operations within the test case behaviour.
requirements.original: The actual configuration of components and the connections between them is achieved by performing create and connect operations within the test case behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:map-operation
requirements.canonical: A port of a test component IS connected to a port of the test system interface by means of the `map` operation.
requirements.original: The component ports are connected to the ports of the test system interface by means of the map operation (see clause 21.1.1).

requirements.subject: ent:connection
requirements.canonical: A connection among test components and between a test component and the test system interface IS port-oriented, i.e. established between ports.
requirements.original: Test components are connected via their ports, i.e. connections among components and between a component and the test system interface are port-oriented.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port IS modelled as an infinite FIFO queue.
requirements.original: Each port is modelled as an infinite FIFO queue which stores the incoming messages or procedure calls until they are processed by the component owning that port (see figure 5).

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port queue IS storing the incoming messages or procedure calls until they are processed by the test component owning that port.
requirements.original: Each port is modelled as an infinite FIFO queue which stores the incoming messages or procedure calls until they are processed by the component owning that port (see figure 5).

ambiguity.issue: 'procedure calls' may be meant literally or as shorthand for all procedure-based communication (calls, replies, exceptions); the broader reading was chosen.
readings: A port queue IS storing incoming messages and all procedure-based items (calls, replies and exceptions) until they are processed by the owning test component.
A port queue IS storing only incoming messages and procedure calls until they are processed by the owning test component.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port of a real test system CAN overflow although TTCN-3 ports are infinite in principle.
requirements.original: NOTE: While TTCN-3 ports are infinite in principle in a real test system they may overflow.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.condition: a port overflows in a real test system
requirements.canonical: An overflow of a port in a real test system SHALL be treated as a test case error.
requirements.original: This is to be treated as a test case error (see clause 24.1).

requirements.subject: ent:connection
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 connection IS either a port-to-port connection or a port-to-test system interface connection.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 connections are port-to-port and port-to-test system interface connections (see figure 6).

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component MAY maintain any number of connections.
requirements.original: There are no restrictions on the number of connections a component may maintain.

requirements.subject: ent:connection
requirements.canonical: A one-to-many connection MAY be established.
requirements.original: One-to-many connections are also allowed (e.g. figure 6 (g) or (h)).

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port owned by a test component A SHALL NOT be connected with two or more ports owned by component A itself.
requirements.original: A port owned by a component A shall not be connected with two or more ports owned by the same component (figure 7 (a) and (e)).

ambiguity.issue: 'the same component' can refer to component A itself or to any single component; since item 9.1-s015 separately covers ports of a different component B, the reading 'component A itself' was chosen.
readings: A port owned by a test component A SHALL NOT be connected with two or more ports owned by component A itself.
A port owned by a test component A SHALL NOT be connected with two or more ports owned by any single test component (A or another one).

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.canonical: A port of the test system interface SHALL NOT be connected with more than one port owned by the same test component.
requirements.original: A port of a test system interface cannot have connection with more than one port owned by a component A. This means, connections as shown in figure 7 (b) are not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port owned by a test component A SHALL NOT be connected with two or more ports owned by another test component B.
requirements.original: A port owned by a component A shall not be connected with two or more ports owned by a component B (see figure 7 (c)).

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port owned by a test component SHALL have at most a one-to-one connection with the test system interface, i.e. it SHALL NOT be connected to more than one port of the test system interface.
requirements.original: A port owned by a component A can only have a one-to-one connection with the test system interface. This means, connections as shown in figure 7 (d) are not allowed.

ambiguity.issue: 'one-to-one' could restrict only the component port side or also the test system interface port side; since one-to-many connections are allowed (figure 6) and 9.1-s014 only restricts ports of the same component, the component-side reading was chosen.
readings: A port owned by a test component SHALL NOT be mapped to more than one port of the test system interface.
A port owned by a test component and the test system interface port it is mapped to SHALL both have no other mapping.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.canonical: A port of the test system interface SHALL NOT be connected with another port of the test system interface.
requirements.original: Connections within the test system interface are not allowed (see figure 7 (f)).

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port that is connected SHALL NOT be mapped.
requirements.original: A port that is connected shall not be mapped and a port that is mapped shall not be connected (see figure 7 (g)).

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port that is mapped SHALL NOT be connected.
requirements.original: A port that is connected shall not be mapped and a port that is mapped shall not be connected (see figure 7 (g)).

requirements.subject: ent:connection
requirements.canonical: The restrictions on connections CANNOT always be checked at compile-time, because TTCN-3 allows dynamic configurations and addresses.
requirements.original: b) Since TTCN-3 allows dynamic configurations and addresses, the restrictions on connections cannot always be checked at compile-time.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL check the restrictions on connections at runtime.
requirements.original: The checks shall be made at runtime and shall lead to a test case error when failing.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether all connection checks or only those that cannot be performed at compile-time shall be made at runtime; the latter reading was chosen as most likely, but the canonical is phrased generally.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL check at runtime those connection restrictions that cannot be checked at compile-time.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL check all connection restrictions at runtime, regardless of compile-time checks.

requirements.subject: ent:test-case-error
requirements.condition: a runtime connection restriction check fails
requirements.canonical: A failing runtime check of a connection restriction SHALL lead to a test case error.
requirements.original: The checks shall be made at runtime and shall lead to a test case error when failing.

requirements.subject: ent:iut
requirements.canonical: The object being tested IS the Implementation Under Test (IUT).
requirements.original: The object being tested is known as the Implementation Under Test or IUT.

requirements.subject: ent:iut
requirements.canonical: An IUT CAN offer direct interfaces for testing.
requirements.original: The IUT may offer direct interfaces for testing or it may be part of system in which case the tested object is known as a System Under Test or SUT.

requirements.subject: ent:sut
requirements.condition: the IUT is part of a system
requirements.canonical: When the IUT is part of a system, the tested object IS the System Under Test (SUT).
requirements.original: The IUT may offer direct interfaces for testing or it may be part of system in which case the tested object is known as a System Under Test or SUT.

requirements.subject: ent:sut
requirements.canonical: In the minimal case the IUT and the SUT ARE equivalent.
requirements.original: In the minimal case the IUT and the SUT are equivalent.

requirements.subject: ent:sut
requirements.canonical: The term SUT IS used in the standard to mean either SUT or IUT.
requirements.original: In the present document the term SUT is used in a general way to mean either SUT or IUT.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The specification of the real physical connection to the SUT IS NOT within the scope of TTCN-3.
requirements.original: However, the specification of the real physical connection is outside the scope of TTCN-3.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A well-defined abstract test system interface SHALL be associated with each test case.
requirements.original: Instead, a well defined (but abstract) test system interface shall be associated with each test case.

ambiguity.issue: This conflicts on its face with 9.2-s023 (test system interface need not be associated when only the MTC is used); the reading that the association may be implicit was chosen.
readings: Each test case SHALL have a test system interface, either explicitly given (system clause) or implicitly defined by the MTC component type.
Each test case SHALL explicitly declare a test system interface.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.canonical: A test system interface definition IS identical to a component type definition.
requirements.original: A test system interface definition is identical to a component definition, i.e. it is a list of all possible communication ports through which the test case is connected to the SUT.

ambiguity.issue: 'component definition' is used where 'component type definition' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.canonical: A test system interface IS a list of all possible communication ports through which the test case is connected to the SUT.
requirements.original: A test system interface definition is identical to a component definition, i.e. it is a list of all possible communication ports through which the test case is connected to the SUT.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.canonical: The test system interface IS statically defining the number and type of the port connections to the SUT during a test run.
requirements.original: The test system interface statically defines the number and type of the port connections to the SUT during a test run.

requirements.subject: ent:connection
requirements.canonical: A connection between the test system interface and a test component IS dynamic.
requirements.original: However, the connections between the test system interface and the TTCN-3 test components are dynamic in nature and may be modified during a test run by using map and unmap operations (see clause 21.1).

requirements.subject: ent:connection
requirements.canonical: A connection between the test system interface and a test component MAY be modified during a test run by using `map` and `unmap` operations.
requirements.original: However, the connections between the test system interface and the TTCN-3 test components are dynamic in nature and may be modified during a test run by using map and unmap operations (see clause 21.1).

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.canonical: A component type definition IS used to define the test system interface.
requirements.original: A component type definition is used to define the test system interface because, conceptually, component type definitions and test system interface definitions have the same form (both are collections of ports defining possible connection points).

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.canonical: A component type definition and a test system interface definition ARE conceptually of the same form, both being collections of ports defining possible connection points.
requirements.original: A component type definition is used to define the test system interface because, conceptually, component type definitions and test system interface definitions have the same form (both are collections of ports defining possible connection points).

requirements.subject: ent:system-component
requirements.condition: a component type is used as a test system interface
requirements.canonical: When a component type is used as a test system interface, the test system interface CANNOT make use of the constants, variables and timers declared in that component type.
requirements.original: When used as test system interfaces, components cannot make use of any constants, variables and timers declared in the component type.

ambiguity.issue: 'cannot make use' can be a rule (referencing such declarations via the system component is an error) or a statement of fact (they are not available / have no effect, cf. 9.2-s025); the factual reading was chosen.
readings: The constants, variables and timers declared in a component type used as test system interface ARE not usable by the test system interface (no effect).
A reference to a constant, variable or timer of a component type used as test system interface SHALL be rejected as an error.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.canonical: A test system interface definition HAS the same syntax as a component type definition.
requirements.original: The same as a component type definition (see clause 6.2.10.1).

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.condition: the test case uses more than one test component
requirements.canonical: A test case using more than one test component SHALL be associated with a component type reference defining the test system interface.
requirements.original: Generally, a component type reference defining the test system interface shall be associated with every test case using more than one test component.

ambiguity.issue: 'Generally' weakens the SHALL; it is unclear whether it is a strict rule or a general guideline with exceptions.
readings: A test case using more than one test component SHALL have a `system` clause referencing a component type.
A test case using more than one test component SHOULD normally have a `system` clause; omitting it is not an error.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.canonical: The ports of the test system interface SHALL be instantiated automatically by the test system together with the MTC when the test case execution starts.
requirements.original: The ports of the test system interface shall automatically be instantiated by the system together with the MTC when the test case execution starts.

requirements.subject: ent:system-operation
requirements.canonical: The `system` operation IS returning the component reference of the test system interface.
requirements.original: The operation returning the component reference of the test system interface is system.

requirements.subject: ent:system-operation
requirements.canonical: The `system` operation SHALL be used to address the ports of the test system interface.
requirements.original: This shall be used to address the ports of the test system.

ambiguity.issue: 'ports of the test system' is used where 'ports of the test system interface' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.condition: the MTC is the only test component instantiated during test execution
requirements.canonical: When the MTC is the only test component instantiated during test execution, a test system interface NEED NOT be associated to the test case.
requirements.original: In the case where the MTC is the only component that is instantiated during test execution, a test system interface need not be associated to the test case.

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.condition: the MTC is the only test component and no test system interface is associated
requirements.canonical: When the MTC is the only test component instantiated during test execution, the component type associated with the MTC IS implicitly defining the test system interface.
requirements.original: In this case, the component type definition associated with the MTC implicitly defines the corresponding test system interface.

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.condition: the component type is used as test system interface
requirements.canonical: A variable, timer or constant declared in a component type that is used as test system interface IS without effect.
requirements.original: Variables, timers and constants declared in component types, which are used as test system interfaces will have no effect.

ambiguity.issue: 'will have no effect' is informal; the plural 'component types' is meant as a component type used as test system interface.

improper_terms.used: Variables, timers and constants declared in component types
improper_terms.proper: component variables, component timers and component constants

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.canonical: A test system interface definition SHALL satisfy the same restrictions as a component type definition.
requirements.original: a) The same as for component type definitions (see clause 6.2.10.1).
